focus: 了 · I ate
prompt: I ate. Mark the eating event as completed, immediately after 吃.
explanation: 了 marks completion here; 过 would describe experience and 着 an ongoing state.

focus: 了 · She bought three tickets
prompt: She bought three tickets. Mark the completed purchase directly after 买.
explanation: 了 follows 买 and precedes the quantity phrase 三张票.
pinyin: Tā mǎi le sān zhāng piào.

focus: 了 · It has become cold now
prompt: It has become cold now. Add the sentence-final change-of-state marker.
explanation: 冷了 reports a new condition, not a completed action.

focus: 了 · The child is three now
prompt: The child is three now. Mark the new situation at the end.
explanation: Sentence-final 了 marks reaching a new age.

focus: 了 · I no longer drink coffee
prompt: I no longer drink coffee. Mark the change at the end.
explanation: 不了 here means the habit has changed; 不 does not prohibit change-of-state 了.

focus: 了 · The train is about to arrive
prompt: The train is about to arrive. Complete 快…了.
explanation: 快…了 describes an approaching event, showing that 了 is not simply past tense.

focus: 了 · I did not eat breakfast yesterday
prompt: I did not eat breakfast yesterday. Keep a neutral report of the uncompleted event; add nothing if needed.
explanation: 没 negates the occurrence of eating. Do not insert perfective 了 in this neutral negative report.

focus: 了 · I drink tea every day
prompt: I drink tea every day. State only the unchanged habit, without adding experience or a new situation.
explanation: An ordinary unchanged habit needs no aspect particle here. Added 了 would change the intended meaning.

focus: 了 · I am going to Beijing tomorrow
prompt: I am going to Beijing tomorrow. Give only this plain future statement, without a change-of-plan nuance.
explanation: A time expression can locate an event in the future without an aspect particle.

focus: 过 · I have never been to Shanghai
prompt: I have never been to Shanghai. Mark experience directly after 去.
explanation: 没去过 denies past experience. Unlike perfective 了, 过 is retained after 没.

focus: 过 · Have you ever eaten hotpot? Mark experience directly after 吃
prompt: Have you ever eaten hotpot? Mark experience directly after 吃.
explanation: 吃过 asks about prior experience, rather than an ongoing meal.

focus: 过 · I have read this book before
prompt: I have read this book before. Insert the experiential marker after 看.
explanation: 看过 describes having the experience of reading this book.
pinyin: Wǒ kàn guo zhè běn shū.

focus: 着 · The door is standing open
prompt: The door is standing open. Add the marker of the maintained state after 开.
explanation: 开着 describes the door remaining open. 开了 instead can report its opening or a new state.

focus: 着 · He is wearing a coat
prompt: He is wearing a coat. Mark the maintained state immediately after 穿.
explanation: 穿着 describes wearing; 穿了 can describe putting the coat on.
pinyin: Tā chuān zhe yí jiàn wàitào.

focus: 着 · She is holding a book
prompt: She is holding a book. Mark the maintained state after 拿.
explanation: 拿着 means holding something, rather than having once taken it.
pinyin: Tā ná zhe yì běn shū.

focus: 着 · He speaks with a smile
prompt: He speaks with a smile. Mark smiling as the accompanying state after 笑.
explanation: 笑着说 presents smiling as accompanying the speech.

focus: 着 · There is a glass of water sitting on the table
prompt: There is a glass of water sitting on the table. Mark the continuing placement after 放.
explanation: 放着 describes the current arrangement on the table.
pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng fàng zhe yì bēi shuǐ.

focus: 的 · I like red clothes
prompt: I like red clothes. Explicitly link 红色 to 衣服 with the attributive marker.
explanation: 的 connects the description 红色 to the noun 衣服.

focus: 的 · This is the book I bought yesterday
prompt: This is the book I bought yesterday. Link the relative clause to 书.
explanation: 我昨天买的 modifies the noun 书.
pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ zuótiān mǎi de shū.

focus: 的 · I want the big one
prompt: I want the big one. Add the nominalizing particle after 大.
explanation: 大的 stands for the big one, with the noun understood from context.

focus: 的 · My mother is a teacher
prompt: My mother is a teacher. An ordinary unmarked family relationship is intended. Select a valid form, with or without 的.
explanation: 我妈妈 and 我的妈妈 are both valid here. 地 and 得 do not mark possession.

focus: 得 · He speaks very clearly
prompt: He speaks very clearly. Link 说 to its degree complement 很清楚.
explanation: 得 follows the verb and introduces the degree or result description.

focus: 得 · I am so tired that I do not want to speak
prompt: I am so tired that I do not want to speak. Link 累 to its result description.
explanation: 累得 introduces the consequence of being tired.
pinyin: Wǒ lèi de bù xiǎng shuōhuà.

focus: 得 · She writes very well
prompt: She writes very well. Link 写 to 很好.
explanation: 写得很好 evaluates the quality of the writing.

focus: 地 · The child smiled happily
prompt: The child smiled happily. Explicitly mark 高兴 as modifying the action 笑.
explanation: 地 introduces the manner before the verb; 得 would belong after a verb.

focus: 地 · Please speak slowly
prompt: Please speak slowly. Accept either the explicit manner marker or its natural omission.
explanation: 慢慢地说 and 慢慢说 are both natural. 得 is not used before 说 here.

focus: 地 · He sits there quietly
prompt: He sits there quietly. Use an explicit manner marker after 安静.
explanation: 安静地 modifies the following action 坐.
pinyin: Tā ānjìng de zuò zài nàli.

focus: 吗 · Are you ready? Add a neutral yes/no question particle at the end
prompt: Are you ready? Add a neutral yes/no question particle at the end.
explanation: 吗 turns this statement into a neutral yes/no question. The existing 了 stays.

focus: 吗 · Where are you going? Give a plain question-word question; no extra conversational nuance
prompt: Where are you going? Give a plain question-word question; no extra conversational nuance.
explanation: 哪里 already asks for the destination. 吗 would not make this the intended neutral where-question.

focus: 吗 · Who is he? Give a plain question-word question
prompt: Who is he? Give a plain question-word question.
explanation: 谁 already supplies the question; no 吗 is needed.

focus: 吗 · Are you going or not? Keep this ordinary A-not-A question
prompt: Are you going or not? Keep this ordinary A-not-A question.
explanation: 去不去 already forms an A-not-A question, so ordinary usage does not add 吗.

focus: 呢 · Where is my phone? Use the short topic-question particle at the end
prompt: Where is my phone? Use the short topic-question particle at the end.
explanation: 我的手机呢 asks about the phone in a context where its location is at issue.

focus: 呢 · She is reading right now
prompt: She is reading right now. Add the sentence-final particle emphasizing the ongoing situation.
explanation: 正在…呢 emphasizes an ongoing activity.

focus: 吧 · Let us go
prompt: Let us go. Soften this suggestion with a sentence-final particle.
explanation: 吧 makes this a suggestion rather than a bare command.

focus: 吧 · You should rest first
prompt: You should rest first. Add the particle that softens the suggestion.
explanation: 吧 can soften a request or suggestion.

focus: 吧 · He should have arrived, I suppose
prompt: He should have arrived, I suppose. Mark tentative confirmation at the end.
explanation: 吧 signals a tentative inference or invites confirmation.

focus: Classifiers · I want two tickets
prompt: I want two tickets. Insert the flat-object classifier before 票.
explanation: 张 counts flat objects such as tickets; 本 counts bound volumes and 条 long or flexible items.

focus: Classifiers · She bought one item of clothing
prompt: She bought one item of clothing. Put its classifier before 衣服.
explanation: 件 counts individual items of clothing in this phrase.
pinyin: Tā mǎi le yí jiàn yīfu.

focus: Classifiers · I bought a pair of trousers
prompt: I bought a pair of trousers. Insert the conventional classifier before 裤子.
explanation: 条 is used for trousers; Chinese treats a pair as 一条裤子.
pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì tiáo kùzi.

focus: Classifiers · There is a bird in the tree
prompt: There is a bird in the tree. Use the animal classifier before 鸟.
explanation: 只 is a conventional classifier for birds and many other animals.
pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu yì zhī niǎo.

focus: Classifiers · There are two cars at the entrance
prompt: There are two cars at the entrance. Insert the vehicle classifier.
explanation: 辆 counts wheeled vehicles such as cars.

focus: Classifiers · This is a teacher
prompt: This is a teacher. Use the respectful classifier for a person before 老师.
explanation: 位 respectfully counts people, including teachers.

focus: Classifiers · There is a tree in the courtyard
prompt: There is a tree in the courtyard. Insert the classifier for trees.
explanation: 棵 counts trees and plants; 颗 counts small round things.
pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yì kē shù.

focus: Classifiers · She found a pearl
prompt: She found a pearl. Insert the classifier for small round objects.
explanation: 颗 is used for pearls; 棵 is used for trees and plants.
pinyin: Tā zhǎodào le yì kē zhēnzhū.

focus: Classifiers · Please say it one more time
prompt: Please say it one more time. Finish the action-count phrase.
explanation: 一次 means one occurrence of an action.

focus: Classifiers · Please read the article all the way through once
prompt: Please read the article all the way through once. Add the measure word for one complete run-through.
explanation: 遍 emphasizes a complete pass through the article.
pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wénzhāng dú yí biàn.

focus: Classifiers · She gave me a flower
prompt: She gave me a flower. Insert the classifier for a blossom.
explanation: 朵 counts individual blossoms.
pinyin: Tā sòng wǒ yì duǒ huā.

focus: Classifiers · I bought a pair of shoes
prompt: I bought a pair of shoes. Insert the classifier specifically counting a pair.
explanation: 双 explicitly counts the pair; 只 would mean one shoe.
pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le yì shuāng xié.

focus: Classifiers · Please give me a cup of water
prompt: Please give me a cup of water. Insert the measure word meaning cup.
explanation: 杯 measures the water by the cup.
pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi shuǐ.

focus: Classifiers · I would like one serving of fried rice
prompt: I would like one serving of fried rice. Insert the serving measure word.
explanation: 份 counts servings of a dish.

focus: Classifiers · I received a letter
prompt: I received a letter. Insert the classifier for letters.
explanation: 封 is the conventional classifier for letters.
pinyin: Wǒ shōudào le yì fēng xìn.

focus: Classifiers · There is a school nearby
prompt: There is a school nearby. Insert the institutional building classifier.
explanation: 所 counts institutions such as schools.

focus: Classifiers · We watched a match
prompt: We watched a match. Insert the classifier for an event or match.
explanation: 场 counts events such as matches.
pinyin: Wǒmen kàn le yì chǎng bǐsài.

focus: Classifiers · This bag of rice weighs five kilograms
prompt: This bag of rice weighs five kilograms. Do not add an extra classifier.
explanation: 公斤 already functions as the unit after 五.
pinyin: Zhè dài mǐ zhòng wǔ gōngjīn.

focus: 的 · It was yesterday that I came
prompt: It was yesterday that I came. Complete the 是…的 construction at the end.
explanation: 是…的 highlights the time of an established event.

focus: 的 · He came by subway
prompt: He came by subway. Complete 是…的 to emphasize the means of travel.
explanation: 是坐地铁来的 emphasizes how he came.
pinyin: Tā shì zuò dìtiě lái de.

focus: 了 · I have already eaten; the relevant situation is now settled
prompt: I have already eaten; the relevant situation is now settled. Add sentence-final 了.
explanation: 已经吃过饭了 combines experience/completion with the current relevance expressed by final 了.
pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng chī guo fàn le.

focus: 了 · He has not returned yet
prompt: He has not returned yet. Keep the ordinary not-yet statement without any added nuance.
explanation: 还没回来 already states that the return has not happened.

focus: 的 · The weather is good
prompt: The weather is good. Keep the ordinary adjective predicate without extra emphasis.
explanation: 很好 is already a complete adjective predicate here; no 的 or 得 is required.

focus: 着 · Please wait seated
prompt: Please wait seated. Mark sitting as the accompanying state after 坐.
explanation: 坐着等 means to wait while seated.
